stem: A nurse observes a breastfeeding session. Which finding is most consistent with a good latch?

options.A: The baby’s mouth is open wide over the areola, the lips are turned outward, and the chin rests against the breast.
options.B: The baby’s lips are tucked inward and the chin remains away from the breast.
options.C: The baby attaches mainly to the nipple tip and repeatedly clicks during sucking.
options.D: The parent has persistent sharp nipple pain and the baby’s cheeks pull inward with each suck.

rationale: CDC breastfeeding guidance lists a wide-open mouth over the areola, lips turned outward, and the chin resting against the breast as signs of a good latch. Inward-curled lips, nipple-only attachment, clicking, or persistent breastfeeding pain are inconsistent with an effective latch and should prompt reassessment. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the key physical signs of an effective breastfeeding latch: wide mouth over the areola, outward-flanged lips, and the infant’s chin against the breast.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Section ‘What are signs of a good latch?’ and ‘What are signs of a bad latch?’ — wide mouth over areola, lips turned out, chin resting against breast; nipple-only suckling, inward-curled lips, pain and coming off breast as poor-latch signs.
source_claim_supported: A good breastfeeding latch includes a wide-open mouth over the areola, outward-turned lips, and the infant’s chin resting against the breast.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — postpartum/newborn health promotion and client education.
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — breastfeeding latch assessment and teaching

options.A: The baby’s mouth is open wide over the areola, the lips are turned outward, and the chin rests against the breast.
options.B: The baby’s lips are tucked inward and the chin remains away from the breast.

source_original.rationale: CDC breastfeeding guidance describes a good latch as a wide-open mouth taking in the areola, lips turned outward, and the chin against the breast. Option A matches those findings. Option B describes inward lips and poor positioning. Option C describes a shallow nipple-only latch and clicking, which suggest ineffective attachment. Option D describes persistent pain and inward cheek movement, findings that warrant latch reassessment.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Newborn Breastfeeding Basics — Signs of a good latch: mouth open wide over areola, lips turned out, chin resting against breast, regular swallowing. CDC page dated 2024-10-18; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15 including current 2026 breastfeeding resources. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance; preventive care, screening, prenatal/postpartum and newborn health-promotion activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: No clinical correction was required. The exact CDC good-latch and bad-latch sections were documented and the rationale was limited to findings explicitly supported by those sections.

audit_findings.currentness: CDC Newborn Breastfeeding Basics page rechecked 2026-08-16; current 2026 breastfeeding resources remain consistent.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Good-latch and bad-latch subsections directly support the tested physical findings.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No feed duration, frequency, milk-transfer threshold, or nipple-treatment rule was added.

distractor_audit.A: Correct and directly matches CDC good-latch criteria.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because inward lips and chin away from the breast are inconsistent with good attachment.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because nipple-only attachment and clicking are poor-latch signs.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because persistent pain is a poor-latch concern rather than a good-latch finding.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains exclusively positive latch findings.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe observable breastfeeding findings with comparable detail.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Health Promotion and Maintenance through breastfeeding assessment and parent teaching.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second-pass review checked each distractor against CDC good/bad latch criteria; no second answer remains.
